title: Tenant-aware graduated A/B runway with per-request exposure throttles
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Objective: Build a first-class A/B experimentation runway that supports tenant-aware graduated exposures and per-request throttles so that we can run safe, cost-conscious model version experiments across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Background: Current model rollout primitives support static traffic slices and simple canaries. We need a framework that can: 1) apply different exposure schedules per customer or tenant (eg. low-risk enterprise tenants vs high-churn startups), 2) throttle exposure at the per-request level for bursty workloads, and 3) integrate sequential statistical checks and automated rollback triggers based on multiple signals (quality, latency, cost). This ticket defines the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and the initial implementation milestones.

Scope:
- Experiment definition UI/DSL for per-tenant and global cohorts.
- Exposure scheduler that supports graded ramps (time-based, event-based, metric-gated) and per-request token budget enforcement.
- Multi-metric sequential testing harness (frequentist alpha-spending + conservative Bayesian fallback).
- Auto-rollback policies with configurable sensitivity and cool-down windows.
- Shadow traffic plumbing for silent comparison and drift checks.

Non-goals:
- Full statistical experimentation service (we will integrate with existing analytics pipelines first).
- Cross-account co-experiments and complex multi-arm bandits (out of scope for initial launch).

Success criteria:
1) Product teams can create a gated A/B rollout that specifies tenant groups with different exposure ramps.
2) Per-request throttle prevents any tenant from exceeding its allocated exposure budget under burst traffic.
3) Statistical checks detect a 5% relative degradation in primary quality metric with >90% power within 24 hours in typical traffic patterns (simulation validated).
4) Auto-rollback can safely revert traffic to baseline model within target SLO (median rollback time < 6 minutes after trigger).

Telemetry & observability needs:
- Per-variant and per-tenant dashboards: exposure %, request rate, latency p50/p95/p99, quality metric distribution, embedding drift score, cost-per-token.
- Statistical engine logs: sequential p-values, Bayesian posterior checks, alpha spend history.
- Rollback incidents stream and runbook links.

Compliance: Customer-tenanted exposures must respect RLZ data boundaries for Private deployments. KMS-based audit trail required for experimental configuration changes in enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Create experiment with tenant-scoped cohorts and assign ramp profiles
Per-request throttle enforces tenant exposure budget under simulated burst traffic
Sequential statistical checks report inline in Console and trigger alert when thresholds are breached
Auto-rollback action documented and executed in staging with median rollback < 6 minutes
Shadow traffic capture available and paired comparison metrics computed automatically
tasks: Finalize DSL for experiment definition (product + engineering design)
Implement exposure scheduler API and datastore (support per-tenant weights and time windows)
Add per-request token bucket throttle in request router and runtime enforcement pathway
Integrate sequential statistical test library and create an observable event stream
Surface experiment controls and metrics in Console; add playbook links for rollbacks
Run canary in staging across 3 tenants and validate simulation scenarios
Document operator runbook and SLOs for rollback/restore flows
risks: False positives from aggressive sequential checks causing unnecessary rollbacks
Per-request throttles could increase tail latency if implemented inline without batching considerations
Tenant segmentation complexity — risk of misconfiguring high-sensitivity policies for enterprise customers
Observability gaps could make root cause analysis slow during rollback windows
proposed_rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review + simulation (2 weeks) — validate alpha spend schedule on historical traffic
Phase 1: Staging integration (3 weeks) — expose feature to internal tenants and run synthetic fail/pass scenarios
Phase 2: Beta with 5 pilot customers (4 weeks) — tenant-aware ramps and live shadow comparisons
Phase 3: Gradual GA (rolling over 6 weeks) — enable default conservative policies and expand tenant opt-in
simulation_results_summary: Initial offline simulations on sample traffic (consolidated from three customers) show the graded ramp plus per-request throttles keeps exposure oscillation under 2% during bursts and lowers rollback false-positive rate by ~40% compared to a fixed-threshold sequential test. Cost model simulations predict ~8-12% token cost savings by early shadowing and gating low-quality cohorts.
open_questions: How should tenant priority be expressed (categorical tiers vs numeric risk score)?
What default alpha spending schedule minimizes detection latency while controlling FDR for multiple metrics?
Should per-request throttles operate on tokens or request-count for streaming endpoints?
How do we expose experiment visibility to enterprise customers without leaking control-plane internals?
